reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1200/month (Aug-Sep) (E-02), driven by a rise in incorrect bills rather than slow ticket handling, since response times remain within SLA (E-03) and no tariff change occurred (E-07). The best-supported, uncontradicted mechanism is a billing import/validation defect since August that is misbilling both estimate-substituted reads and bills carrying ACTUAL reads (H-RULE-CHANGE-MISBILLING, supported by E-04, 59% of disputed bills are ACTUAL-read), compounded by field manual-read route completion falling to 88% against a 95% target across 9,200 accounts since August (E-01).
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1,200/month (Aug-Sep) (E-02); this is not driven by slow ticket handling, since response times remain within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d, E-03), nor by a tariff change, which did not occur this year (E-07). For the 1,240 disputed bills carrying an ESTIMATED read (41% of 3,025 disputes, E-04), authoritative AMI read-event data shows 1,184 (95%) had a valid read delivered and exported but REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION at billing import (E-11); this traces to billing-import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, which compares raw register values to 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling (E-13), misreading firmware-v4.2 meters' 0.1 m3 sub-unit reads (rolled out June 2026) as roughly 10x actual consumption and triggering rejection and estimate substitution (E-12).
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
